A.strength: languages/tools line leads the page; Boston Dynamics under a robotics header
A.weakness: Emerson manufacturing internship and top-of-page CAD/hardware line make it read as a mechanical engineer for an SDE role

B.strength: one-line summary ('robotics software... in C++', 'on Atlas at Boston Dynamics') shows fit instantly; tight, no padding
B.weakness: cute bullet labels ('Proved it before trusting it') and no data structures, OOD or AWS signal

C.strength: Boston Dynamics leads with the software deliverable (pipeline, ETL, dashboard used by test engineers)
C.weakness: every bullet starts with a number; '100x vs IMU-only' and '0.8% vs 98% feed-forward' compare against trivially weak baselines

D.strength: most technical depth at Boston Dynamics (delta-v metric checked against synthetic pulses and a noise floor)
D.weakness: skills block stuffed with controls keywords; templated labels and 'real-time' wording on a simulation-only filter

E.strength: states 'available Summer 2027'; 'on the real robot', 'v1 board fabricated' and 'ESP32 build in CI' remove the sim-vs-hardware doubt
E.weakness: CATIA fixtures, the Emerson CNC/GD&T internship and CNC/GD&T skills push it toward a mechanical profile

F.strength: Boston Dynamics and the C++ embedded controller are still visible
F.weakness: legged C++ estimator cut to one plain bullet, no tests/CI or code link; hobbies, CAD and FEA padding; crowded old-style layout

G.strength: clear build-then-result C++ estimator story with verification (finite-difference Jacobians, 1e-13 match to a Python reference, observability)
G.weakness: skills at the bottom and kinematics bullets ahead of the software pipeline, so SDE fit shows up slowly

notes: The top versions framed the candidate as a robotics software engineer: C++ with testing and verification, the Boston Dynamics data pipeline, and simulation work clearly labeled. They also cut mechanical padding. The bottom versions spent space on CAD, manufacturing and hobbies, or squeezed the C++ estimation and testing work into vague one-liners, which matters for an SDE role held by a non-CS major.
